correctness.rationale: All-size derivation checked term by term. Given the complete induced graph H, only edges outside its h-vertex set are random. Conditional indicator multiplicities for 0/1/2/3 internal vertices are C(N,3), h C(N,2), eN, and deterministic t; diagonals contribute C(N,3)+hC(N,2) copies with variance p^3-p^6 and eN with p^2-p^4. Every pair of distinct triangles has at most one common edge; covariance is nonzero exactly when it is random. Six exhaustive overlap classes contribute pair numbers C(N,2)C(N-2,2), h C(N,2)(N-2) twice, C(h,2)C(N,2), 2eN(N-1), and Nw. Multiplying their Bernoulli covariances by two gives formula (1). The last pair class alone depends on w; subtraction at fixed e proves gap and strictness. Boundary N=0,1 and p=0,1 correctly vanish as appropriate. Standalone exact exhaustive free-edge enumeration and structural examples independently pass 612 rational assertions; finite computation is corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Statement/implication-level comparison with three accessible primary full-text sources and closely related mathematical claims found no directly covering induced-graph-conditioned triangle variance theorem. Ellis–Ferry and Kunegis establish unconditional motif-count second moments, Ginoza–Mugler analyze a different randomization process, and a related published finding gives a fixed-edge conditional mean rather than a variance. The explicit wedge-only dependence, exact equal-edge gap and smallest claw/path distinction are not their stated results. The broader general overlap framework could implicitly entail this by a specialized derivation and is retained as genuine residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Exact conditional variance may be implicit in older general two-copy overlap/edge-exposure identities that were not explicitly enumerated for observed induced graphs; novelty is best-knowledge rather than certified globally.
No independent expert priority check, and comprehensive historical indexing cannot be guaranteed.
No claim that a finite enumeration is itself an all-size proof.

value.rationale: Triangle counts are standard clustering observables whose residual variability matters under partial observation of a network. Conditional mean depends on observed internal triangle count and edge count, but conditional variance collapses to edge and wedge counts, an exact structural second-moment phenomenon with an all-parameter strict ordering. The four-vertex path/claw provides a minimal connected equal-edge, triangle-free witness with identical conditional expectation but different variance for every n>4 and 0<p<1. This is a natural nontrivial invariant and sharp finite-sample distinction rather than a routine renamed unconditional moment or arbitrary numerical slice; downstream testing gain is not asserted.
